newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metsa-Botnia says refrains from pulp price hike.
newsitem.headline: Metsa-Botnia says refrains from pulp price hike.

text.p: Pulp maker Metsa-Botnia, jointly owned by Finnish forestry firms Metsa-Serla Oy and UPM-Kymmene Oy, said on Friday it would refrain from a planned pulp price hike following disappointing Norscan data.

"We will not do anything for the time being," Metsa-Botnia marketing director Jyrki Yrjo-Koskinen told Reuters when asked whether Metsa-Botnia would hike its pulp price despite a rise in North American and Scandinavian (Norscan) pulp inventories.
Yrjo-Koskinen said Norscan inventories rose 183,000 tonnes to more than 1.9 million tonnes in in November, which was a "slight disappointment".
Metsa-Botnia said earlier this week it was likely to follow foreign pulp producers and raise the price of softwood market pulp to $610 per tonne from $560 at the beginning of 1997.
Inventories particularly in North America were "excessive", while inventories is Scandinavia were at a "normal" level, Yrjo-Koskinen said.
Norscan pulp inventories traditionally tend to rise in November and fall in December, he said.
